answer: An agent gains influence only by locking a scarce, nontransferable bond. Randomly assigned tasks and public challenge proofs can expose accounts controlled by one operator; if a challenge verifies the link, the linked bonds are slashed. This does not make sybils impossible, but each extra identity ties up capital and raises the amount at risk, while one proven cluster can lose its stake. The crystal rule is simple: basalt anchors a thread of costly accountability.
